chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who lends money to another man for one year, or two years, or three years, or whatever God wills. Is the zakat on the lender or the borrower? He said: 'On the borrower, because he derives benefit from it, so the zakat is upon him.'
ai.seo_question: Who is responsible for paying zakat on a loaned amount: the lender or the borrower?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that zakat on a loan falls upon the borrower because they derive the primary benefit (naf'ah) from the capital, a principle that distinguishes this ruling from other debt scenarios in Shia jurisprudence. This hadith, found in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, provides the foundational logic for the distribution of zakat liability in commercial transactions, emphasizing the link between benefit and obligation.
